vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: the counter in a hotel where you arrive and ask for help
the paper or the file that proves you paid, with the amount on it
free to be used or taken at that moment
extra waiting time, when something happens later than planned

the moment you arrive and the hotel gives you your room
what you say when something is wrong and you want somebody to fix it

reading.rtitle: The Night the Room Was Not There
paras: The ferry from Split arrived two hours late, so I reached the hotel close to midnight. The lobby was empty. The man at the front desk was polite and very tired, and after a long minute he told me that he could not find my reservation anywhere on the screen. I had paid for that room in June.

There are two ways to spend the next five minutes, and I have tried both in my life. That night I chose the quiet one. I said that I was afraid there might be a problem with the booking, and I asked whether he could check the number instead of the name. I had the receipt on my phone, from June, with the number on it. It took him forty seconds. The reservation was there, spelled with one different letter.

The room I booked was not available any more, but he had an alternative on the top floor, smaller and much quieter. He offered it before I asked for it. I am certain that the words did that, and not the paper. A complaint tells somebody that they have a problem. A question gives them something to solve. So my advice for a late check-in is short: keep the receipt where you can find it in ten seconds, learn to say would it be possible, and remember that a delay is not the same thing as a disaster.

bank.label: Useful sentences at a front desk or a table
items: I am afraid there might be a problem with my reservation.
Could you check the name again, please? I have the receipt here.
Could I check in a little later? My ferry is delayed.
I would like a room with a view of the harbor, if one is available.
Would it be possible to move the reservation to Thursday instead?
Is it possible to leave the bags at the front desk until three?
I am not making a complaint. I just need an alternative.
Could I have the receipt, please? I need it for the office.

listenings.text: I work the night shift at the front desk, so let me tell you exactly what happens here. Around eleven the ferry people start arriving, all of them tired, and half of them with a reservation I cannot find on the first try. Here is the part nobody believes. The guest who says could you check the name again, please, gets a room faster than the guest who makes a speech. It is not because I like him more. It is because I can actually listen. And if the room really is gone, I almost always have an alternative somewhere in the building: a smaller one, a higher one, a quieter one. But I offer it to the people who ask me a question, not to the people who bring me a complaint. So if your check-in goes wrong at midnight, use ten words instead of a hundred, and keep the receipt where you can find it.

My advice comes from one very bad night in Split. The ferry was two hours late, the evening shift had already gone home, and the man on duty told me there was no reservation under my name. I had paid in June. What saved me was not my temper. It was a photograph. I had the receipt on my phone, with the booking number on it, and I asked him one question: could you check that number for me, please. It took him forty seconds. The reservation was there, spelled with a different letter. So now I do three things before every trip. I save the receipt as a photograph, I write the booking number on paper as well, and I learn how to say would it be possible in the local language. Two of those three have never failed me.

extra_audio.text: First the ferry from Split arrived two hours late, and he reached the hotel close to midnight. Then the man at the front desk looked for his name on the screen and could not find the reservation anywhere. After that he opened the photograph of the receipt on his phone and asked whether the man could check the booking number instead. At that point the reservation appeared, spelled with one different letter, but the original room was no longer available. In the end they gave him an alternative on the top floor, smaller and much quieter, and he decided that the delay had been worth it.
